scope: Initial focused/risk review measurements and a threshold decision; controlled demo tasks with real provider responses.

decision.reason: Measured boundaries and the small sensitive change selected the expected reviewers. The observed failures concerned handoff instructions, a report reader, queue capacity, and interpretation of a staged request. This small, prompted sample does not justify changing size or file limits.

measurement_method.responses: Real BB protected-worker provider calls; no scripted provider replies.
measurement_method.case_duration: Wall time from setup through result and cleanup.
measurement_method.review_duration: Sum of matched started/completed events for each review step and attempt; includes output corrections and scheduling inside the step.
measurement_method.source: Every passing case checks its own commit and tracked-diff hash before and after execution. Passing cases span two commits; the risk policy is unchanged.
measurement_method.oracle: Exact documentation bytes, public function behavior, reviewer selection, saved finding resolution, current content version, effective settings, one dispatch per operation, and stopped owned containers.
measurement_method.review_feedback: Task-assistant assessment explicitly labelled as such; not an independent human or blind review.

limits: One model, one local BB/worker setup, and a small demo target.
All roles are told about the staged defect; this is not blind defect-detection recall.
Four documentation size cases use exact examples, not representative large code changes.
The 20/21-file boundary and ordinary generated-file handling have controlled tests, not live measurements in this study.
No claim of a general false-positive rate, optimal thresholds, token cost, or causal speed improvement.
Concurrent live groups exhausted available BB execution slots; remaining groups ran sequentially.
PR delivery is verified by controlled GitHub adapter tests; this study does not establish live controller publication or review-fix acceptance.
